''' Romane Lewis Clark''' (December 3, 1925 – August 17, 2007) was an American philosopher and Professor Emeritus of Philosophy at [[Indiana University, Bloomington]]. He is known for his works on [[logic]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Baylis |first1=Charles A. |title=Romane Clark. More on negation. Philosophical Studies, vol. 4 (1953), pp. 81–87. |journal=The Journal of Symbolic Logic |date=March 1955 |volume=20 |issue=1 |pages=59–60 |doi=10.2307/2268056 |jstor=2268056 |s2cid=123733524 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-symbolic-logic/article/abs/romane-clark-more-on-negation-philosophical-studies-vol-4-1953-pp-8187/5AC0235F0B2ECB16EAC276F2E570A87D |language=en |issn=0022-4812|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=MEMORIAL RESOLUTION – ROMANE L. CLARK – 1925-2007 |url=https://institutionalmemory.iu.edu/aim/bitstream/handle/10333/10788/B6-2009.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Shook |first1=John R. |title=Dictionary of Modern American Philosophers |year=2005 |publisher=A&C Black |isbn=978-1-84371-037-0 |page=500 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ijpj1tB3Qr0C&dq=Romane+Clark+1925&pg=PA500 |language=en}}</ref> especially his eponymous paradox ([[Abstract object theory#Overview|Clark's paradox]]).<ref>Romane Clark, "Not Every Object of Thought has Being: A Paradox in Naive Predication Theory", ''Noûs'' '''12'''(2) (1978), pp. 181–188.</ref><ref>Adriano Palma, ed. (2014). [https://books.google.com/books?id=iYHoBQAAQBAJ&dq= ''Castañeda and his Guises: Essays on the Work of Hector-Neri Castañeda'']. Boston/Berlin: Walter de Gruyter, pp. 67–82, esp. 71.</ref>

==Books==
* Romane Clark and Paul Welsh, ''Introduction to Logic'', Princeton, N.J., Toronto, New York, London: D. Van Nostrana Company, Inc., 1962.
